title: How to Track Expenses in Google Sheets (Free Template)

body:
Most people who say they have no idea where their money goes are right. Card payments, transfers and small cash purchases blur together, and the bank app shows a list, not a picture. An expense tracker fixes that. You log each purchase with a category, and the sheet adds up how much went where. After one month you will know your real numbers, which is what every budget needs. Here is a free one for Google Sheets, with a step-by-step guide.

Download the free expense tracker (.xlsx)

No sign-up and no email needed. It also works in Excel. ![The Summary tab of the expense tracker, showing spending by category for October with each category's share of the total](/assets/img/posts/expense-tracker-preview-980x830.webp) ## What's inside the tracker | Tab | What it does | |---|---| | Start here | Five short steps | | Summary | Pick a month and see the total for each category, its share of spending, your biggest category and how many purchases you made | | Transactions | One line per purchase: date, description, category, amount and how you paid | **Yellow cells** are for you to type in. **White cells** calculate by themselves. ## How to set it up in Google Sheets 1. Download the file with the button above. 2. In [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/), choose **New**, then **File upload**, and pick the file. 3. Double-click it, then choose **File**, then **Save as Google Sheets**. 4. Install the Google Sheets app on your phone and open the file there once. Logging a purchase on your phone takes about ten seconds. In Excel, just open the downloaded file. ## How to track your expenses ### 1. Set your categories On the **Summary** tab, the yellow cells in the Category column are yours to rename. The examples are Rent, Groceries, Eating out, Transport, Bills, Shopping, Fun and Other, with two spare rows. Keep it to around eight to ten categories. Too few and you learn nothing. Too many and logging becomes a chore. If you already have a budget, use the same categories so the two line up. ### 2. Log every purchase On the **Transactions** tab, add one line for each purchase: - **Date**, typed like `2026-10-14` - **Description**, a few words such as "Weekly shop" - **Category**, chosen from the dropdown so the spelling always matches - **Amount** - **Paid with**, such as cash, debit card or bank transfer (optional, but useful for spotting which card does the damage) The example rows show the format. Delete them when you start. ### 3. Pick the month to look at On the Summary tab, type the first day of a month next to **Month starting**, for example `2026-10-01`. Every total on the page updates to that month only. Type an earlier month to look back. ### 4. Read the summary For the chosen month, you see: - how much you spent in each category - what share of your total spending each category is - your total, your biggest category and your number of purchases ## A worked example The file comes with ten example purchases. One of them is from September 28, so it is left out when the month is set to October. The other nine give this October summary: | Category | Spent | Share | |---|---:|---:| | Rent | $450.00 | 64.0% | | Groceries | $103.40 | 14.7% | | Transport | $65.00 | 9.2% | | Bills | $35.00 | 5.0% | | Eating out | $22.70 | 3.2% | | Shopping | $15.00 | 2.1% | | Fun | $12.00 | 1.7% | | **Total** | **$703.10** | **100%** | Rent takes almost two thirds of the spending, which is common on a small income. That is useful to know: it means the flexible categories have less room than they seem, and that [cutting the grocery bill](/blog/save-money-on-groceries-without-coupons/) or the small extras matters more than it would on a bigger income. ## How the formulas work Each category total uses `SUMIFS` with three conditions: the category matches, the date is on or after the first of the month, and the date is before the first of the next month. ``` =SUMIFS(Transactions!$D$5:$D$2000, Transactions!$C$5:$C$2000, A6, Transactions!$A$5:$A$2000, ">="&$B$3, Transactions!$A$5:$A$2000, "<"&EDATE($B$3,1)) ``` `EDATE($B$3,1)` means "the same day one month later", so the sheet never needs to know how many days a month has. The share is each total divided by the overall total. The biggest category uses `INDEX` and `MATCH` to find the row with the largest amount, and the number of purchases uses `COUNTIFS` with the same two date conditions. If you'd like to understand `SUMIFS` properly, our [SUMIF and SUMIFS guide](/blog/sumifs-google-sheets/) has seven examples you can practise on. ## Tips that keep you tracking - **Log within a day.** It is easy to remember yesterday's coffee. It is hard to remember last Tuesday's. - **Use your banking app as a backup.** Once a week, scroll through your transactions and add anything you missed. Cash is the usual gap, so log cash straight away. - **Don't judge the first month.** The goal is an honest picture, not a perfect one. Change nothing at first. Just record. - **Turn the numbers into a plan.** After a month, use your real totals to set the amounts in the [free monthly budget template](/blog/free-budget-template-google-sheets/). - **Look back once a month.** The [20-minute monthly money review](/blog/monthly-money-review/) is a simple routine for doing that. ## Spreadsheet or app? Apps can pull in your bank transactions automatically, which saves typing. But many of the good ones charge, only work in some countries, or need access to your bank login. Typing your own spending is slower, but it is free, private, and makes you notice each purchase. If you would rather have an app, our [comparison of free budgeting apps](/blog/best-free-budgeting-apps/) looks at what each one really offers for free. ## Frequently asked questions **Is the tracker free?** Yes. Download it, change it and share it. **How long does tracking take?** About a minute a day, or five minutes every couple of days with your banking app open. **Can I track more than one month?** Yes. Keep adding lines on the Transactions tab. It has room for about a thousand purchases, and the Summary tab can show any month. **Does it work offline?** Excel works offline. Google Sheets can work offline in Chrome or Edge if you turn on offline access while you are online. Our [Google Sheets vs Excel guide](/blog/google-sheets-vs-excel-budgeting/) covers the details. **Can I add a category later?** Yes. Type it in one of the spare rows on the Summary tab and it appears in the dropdown. *This tracker is general information, not financial advice. The example numbers are made up to show the format.* ## Sources - [SUMIFS function, Google Docs Editors Help](https://support.google.com/docs/answer/3238496)
